themes_detail.label: Water Quality Crisis This Week
themes_detail.summary: Water quality complaints spiked to 3 reports THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.2 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 1100% surge—raising urgent questions about tap water safety or contamination events in Morningside Heights/Hamilton Heights.
evidence: 3 water quality complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (8-week average)
Z-score of 6.35 indicates statistically significant anomaly
No prior local news coverage or community board agenda items explaining cause
Complaints emerged suddenly with no preceding pattern
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Environmental Protection: have there been water main breaks, boil-water advisories, or contamination reports in the district this week?
Interview affected residents: are they experiencing discoloration, odor, or taste changes in tap water?
Cross-check with NYC Health Department on any water-related illness clusters or advisories

themes_detail.label: Street Lighting Outages Surge
themes_detail.summary: Street light condition complaints jumped to 31 reports LAST WEEK, a 428% increase over the prior 8-week average of 5.9 per week, suggesting widespread outages or delayed repairs affecting public safety and visibility across the neighborhood.
evidence: 31 street light complaints last week vs. 5.9 weekly average over 8 weeks
Z-score of 7.08 indicates highly significant statistical spike
Community board has historically requested transportation/infrastructure funding, suggesting ongoing maintenance gaps
No recent news coverage explaining the cause
reporting_angles: Request DEP/NYCDOT maintenance logs: how many street lights are currently out in CD 109? What is the repair timeline?
Document the outages geographically: which blocks or neighborhoods are darkest? Interview residents about safety concerns.
Investigate whether this is part of a citywide outage or isolated to Morningside Heights/Hamilton Heights

themes_detail.label: Park Rules Violations Explode
themes_detail.summary: Violation of Park Rules complaints spiked to 4 reports LAST WEEK, a staggering 3100% increase over an 8-week baseline of 0.1 per week, indicating a sudden shift in park usage patterns, enforcement, or specific incidents requiring immediate investigation.
evidence: 4 park rules violation complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (8-week average)
Z-score of 11.72, the highest statistical severity on the data set
Complaints emerged suddenly with no prior escalation pattern
Community board has repeatedly requested park upgrades, suggesting existing maintenance/use issues
reporting_angles: Which parks are generating complaints? Interview NYC Parks enforcement and neighborhood residents about what behavior has changed.
Are these complaints tied to a specific incident (e.g., unsafe activity, large gatherings, substance use) or ongoing patterns?
Cross-check with police/non-emergency reports: have there been related crime or safety complaints at these parks?

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk Noise Doubles in One Week
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints surged to 152 reports LAST WEEK, a 260% spike over the 8-week average of 42.2 per week, suggesting construction, street events, or a new noise source has emerged in the neighborhood.
evidence: 152 street/sidewalk noise complaints last week vs. 42.2 weekly average over 8 weeks
Z-score of 4.78 indicates significant statistical anomaly
Residential noise complaints (1,396 total over 90 days) remain elevated overall, but street-level noise is new driver
No recent news coverage explaining trigger for spike
reporting_angles: Interview 311 callers and residents: what specific noise sources are they reporting? Construction, traffic, music, or something else?
Cross-check NYC Department of Buildings permit data: are there new construction projects or street work authorized in the district?
Map complaint locations: is the noise geographically concentrated (e.g., near Columbia University) or dispersed?

themes_detail.label: Lost Property Reports Spike
themes_detail.summary: Lost property complaints tripled THIS WEEK to 3 reports versus a 0.4 weekly baseline, a 700% increase suggesting potential theft, security gaps, or a sudden spike in foot traffic or vulnerable populations in the district.
evidence: 3 lost property complaints this week vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (8-week average)
Z-score of 5.42 indicates statistically significant spike
Complaints emerged suddenly with no preceding trend
Limited context: unclear whether losses are related to theft, negligence, or public space insecurity
reporting_angles: Contact NYPD: have there been related robbery, burglary, or theft complaints this week? Is there a pattern?
Investigate where losses occurred: public transit, parks, streets, or businesses? What types of items?
Interview residents and business owners: do they perceive increased theft or security concerns?
